name: lance_encoding::encodings::logical::primitive::dict::dict_encode_variable_width
behavior: Generic variable-width dictionary helper borrows block bytes, typed offsets and U8SliceKey map entries. Stat MaxLength must exist and be a UInt64 array; expect panics otherwise. Initial payload capacity is saturating32*max_length, at least1024, then bounded by source data and target budget. Indices reserve declared num_values. No complete offset-count/first-zero/final-end validation. Iterate every physical adjacent offset pair; conversion to usize, descending offsets or end beyond data return None. Nonzero first offset or unused trailing data are accepted. Exact byte strings map to first-seen signed i32 IDs. New entry requires positive max_entries, current unique count below it and below i32::MAX. Payload is extended before output-offset conversion and size checks, so rejected attempts still allocate transiently. After each index, estimated encoded size is saturating payload bytes +4*index count +offset-width*(unique count+1). Return None only when greater than max_encoded_size, allowing equality. This is an output-size filter, not peak-memory bound: map, preallocation, stats and allocations before checks are excluded. No loop iterations bypasses this in-loop size check. Successful variable-width result has dictionary offsets/data and unique count with matching32/64 offset width, plus FixedWidth indices with32 bits and declared input num_values. Statistics are recomputed for both. Physical window count is not compared with declared num_values, so malformed blocks can yield inconsistent counts.
